Results.ReviewText:
A lot of people get so excited about this grill that that they *have* to write about it after just a few days' use. This covers a somewhat longer timeline than that.

My experience with Weber grills practically goes back to childhood, but nearly all those were charcoal grills. When me and my wife finally over into a decent-sized house, one of the things on my mind was grilling, but I was all about cooking with gas, for a number of reasons, and the only name on my radar was Weber. The E-210 was the perfect size - neither too-much or too-little grill. As soon as we got it, and placed it on the back deck of the house, I went to town like never before, and the grill has consistently delivered the goods, year-round. (Appreciated the recent piece about winter grilling…I feel a little less like a weirdo now.) Have read some of the criticisms of the grill here, and have a few observations:

- I regard the Flavorizer bars as something of a semi-consumable: since I use the grill on the average of 3-4 days a week, I've clocked a *lot* of hors on the thing, and I'm frankly amazed the bars lasted as long as they did (four years). Just replaced them this past summer.

- Igniter: I can only speak for myself, but I have yet to replace even the battery on the original igniter…and this on a grill that stays outside year-round (and doesn't always get its cover put on as it should; my bad.)

In all, I can't imagine being without this grill. Everything I've always known tastes better when grilled is now absolutely scrumptious. Wife doesn't make fun of me when I go grilling in snow, because she knows she getting good eats as well. I'm sure there are other decent grills around, but I go with what I know here. Heartily recommended.
Results.Title: Five-Year Reflections

Results.ReviewText: We purchased an earlier version of this grill several years ago, and loved it. It is not cheap, but held up very well despite nearly daily useage. (Love that California Living!)  Because it is a Weber, it is possible to find replacement parts, and we did have to replace the flavor bars and some other items over the years. When we moved recently, we decided we did not have the space to pack/ship the BBQ and promised ourselves we would buy another once we were settled.  And, we did. First, we are extremely happy with the grill.  It is a perfect size for a small family, heats up fast, and cooks reliably.  The starter system has been upgraded since our original model, now with a battery and works even on cold/wet days (original was a striker type, and sometimes if it was really wet outside, it would require a lighter to start).  The grates are high quality cast iron, and has both a wide side and a narrow (we always use the wide side up) so if you are grilling say, asparagus, that helps.  It has a built in propane gas level gage as well, and the mounting system for the tank has also improved and is easier to get the tank mounted inside the base of the BBQ. The other improvement is a switch from a "cosmetic panel" in front to an actual door. Again, much easier to access the area under the grill with a nice hinged door.  Where the grill lost ground over the earlier model is that the original one came with a cast iron griddle that fit into the grate system.  I normally did not bother removing the grate to mount the cast iron pan into the grates, but used the round pan/griddle extensively (I saved the one I had and can now use on the new grill). This was perfect for grilling things like lamb chops and getting an amazing sear, and was my favorite way to cook a spatchcocked chicken.  The pan was a really nice perk, but the problem now with the grill grates is that there are little nubbie protrusions on the grates to keep them separated and spaced, but it leaves too wide a gap between the two grates. Kind of have to cook on one side or the other, or cook something pretty big so it doesn't go through the gap. I could dock my rating by one star for that, but I haven't seen any better grills out there, so can't really penalize the product for a past rendition being better.
Results.Title: Still the best small bbq around

Results.ReviewText:
We are generally pleased with our new Weber grill. 

Replacing the tank is one royal pain in the back. Because it must be hung on the tank bracket inside the cabinet, it requires two people to lift it onto the bracket. One where the cabinet opens and another reaching through from the back. This is the only way to be able to roll the unit around. If you don't hang it, then it rests on the ground inside the cabinet due to the hole that accommodates the tank. Another model allows the tank to be hung on the outside, but we don't like that option.

If the grill will be outside on a deck or lanai, we recommend getting the optional cover. Rain, etc. will leave water stains on the chrome side tables, the lid and the control panel. Mild liquid soap and warm water (as recommended) removes most of it. Perhaps a stainless steel cleaner will remove what is left.

Allow extra time to preheat the grill and for cooking. It seems to take a lot longer than the Ducane we replaced with the Weber. In fairness, the Ducane had four burners. (Ducane is now owned by Weber.)
Results.Title: Replacing the tank is a pain.
